dominant_variable: Whether expense discipline and core ad monetization could recover faster than the market expected while Reality Labs losses remained bounded enough for consolidated margins and FCF to re-accelerate.
business_thesis: Historical analogue: a broken thesis can become investable again when the dominant variables genuinely change. Meta's 2022 deterioration was followed by explicit cost discipline and a large recovery in revenue growth and operating margin.
counter_thesis: A rebound could have been only cyclical or multiple-driven if ad demand recovered without durable cost discipline, or if Reality Labs and AI capex absorbed the restored operating leverage.
market_expectation_assessment: Retrospective reconstruction. The case is useful because 'correct avoid' in 2022 should not become a permanent exclusion once evidence on costs, margins and revenue trend reverses.
valuation_framework: Compare the depressed 2022 earnings/FCF expectations with normalized ad revenue growth, consolidated operating margin, capex intensity and FCF after the Year of Efficiency. Treat multiple re-rating as secondary to earnings-revision evidence.
kill_criteria: Revenue reacceleration fades while expense growth reaccelerates.
Operating margin improvement reverses without offsetting long-duration growth evidence.
AI and Reality Labs investment grows materially faster than monetization and FCF.
Valuation re-rates materially faster than durable earnings revisions.
unresolved_evidence_gaps: Exact contemporaneous 2022-2023 consensus distributions are not fully persisted.
No contemporaneous TRQuant recommendation is asserted.

provenance.note: historical analogue created in 2026; not evidence of contemporaneous TRQuant recommendation
